evidence_quotes.quote: in-depth discussions among urban governance stakeholders in Kigali between September 2017 – December 2018 and a review of the literature on sanitation in Kigali.
Efforts to improve sanitation for residents in informal settlements in Kigali are hampered by three main challenges: lack of a central sewerage management and treatment system
While there are strategies laid down to deal with sanitation issues in the upcoming Kigali masterplan of 2020, measures such as strengthened awareness at local level will be necessary.

raw_response.plain_vs_narrow_note: Under plain Criterion 2, the study clearly engages with urban governance, municipal master-planning (Kigali masterplan of 2020), and public policy/funding initiatives (c2_legal_admin_plain = yes), whereas under the narrow rule-type Criterion 2 reading it is unclear from the abstract alone whether specific planning, tenure, regulatory, or financing rules governing informal-settlement sanitation access are analysed versus generic infrastructure deficits and awareness measures (c2_legal_admin_narrow = unclear). Both readings yield an overall Phase 5 verdict of unsure because full-text inspection is also required to determine whether the stakeholder discussions and literature synthesis constitute primary qualitative empirical research or a systematic review (c3 = unclear).
raw_response.rationale: The paper addresses liquid and solid waste sanitation access for residents of informal settlements in Kigali, Rwanda (c1 = yes, c4 = yes). However, full-text review is required on two grounds: (1) under the narrow Criterion 2 reading, it is unclear whether the analysis of informal settlements, public funding, and the Kigali masterplan of 2020 examines specific legal, planning/tenure, regulatory, or subsidy/financing rules rather than general infrastructure shortfalls and local awareness; and (2) under Criterion 3, it is unclear whether the 'in-depth discussions among urban governance stakeholders' and 'review of the literature' represent systematic qualitative empirical data or a narrative policy-community synthesis. Per Phase 5 protocol rules against prematurely excluding ambiguous informal-settlement governance abstracts, the record is retained as unsure.
